pageCache.text:
Our Vision & Ethos
Opening doors, inspiring ambition.
Buxton opens doors for our community. We are an honest, kind family of learners, inspiring ambition for our pupils’ futures.
At Buxton School, we believe that every pupil can be inspired to be the very best that they can be. We have integrity; aiming to for all children and young people to become high achievers and kind, active citizens in our ever-changing world.
We are passionate about our pupils’ futures, setting the highest of expectations so that in our supportive community, pupils will develop the skills, confidence, and independence necessary to become successful learners. Our aim is that every pupil will be empowered and inspired to learn and to make outstanding progress through excellent teaching.
We are ambitious for our pupils and the role that they will play in the future of their local and global communities. One of the great strengths of our school is its vibrant diversity, a reflection of the great city in which we live. We are principled in our decision making to ensure that all young people can learn and work together, developing the skills to become future leaders.
Buxton School is a family at the heart of our community. Together with parents, we will enable every pupil to fulfil their potential. This is within a secure and caring environment where we strive to ensure that every pupil will develop a sense of pride, enjoyment and ownership in their school.
Our Vision & Ethos

pageCache.text:
Welcome
We are delighted to welcome you to Buxton School. At Buxton School we believe that every child can be inspired to be the very best that they can be. We have integrity, aiming for all children and young people to become high achievers and kind, active citizens in our ever changing world. We are passionate about our childrens’ futures, setting the highest of expectations so that in our supportive community, children will develop the skills, confidence and independence necessary to become successful learners.
Our aim is that every child will be empowered and inspired to learn and to make outstanding progress through excellent teaching. We are ambitious for our children and the role that they will play in the future of their local and global communities. One of the great strengths of our school is its vibrant diversity, a reflection of the great city in which we live. We are principled in our decision making to ensure that all children can learn and work together, developing the skills to become future leaders. Buxton School is a family at the heart of our community. Together with parents we will enable every child to fulfil their potential. This is within a secure and caring environment where we strive to ensure that every child will develop a sense of pride, enjoyment and ownership of their school. We expect everyone who studies or works at Buxton, including parents and carers, to support our values and work collaboratively to ensure the future success of our children.
We look forward to working with you.
Mrs J Bowers-Broadbent - Headteacher

Artsmark - Gold
We have been awared an Artsmark Gold award!
What is Artsmark?
"Artsmark empowers teachers with the skills they need to embed arts, culture and creativity across the whole curriculum. Our world-leading teacher CPD is delivered by Goldsmiths, University of London.
Schools are recognised for their exceptional commitment to creativity with the Artsmark Award, accredited by Arts Council England – the only award for arts and culture provision in England.
Artsmark is open to primary, secondary and special schools, as well as hospital schools, pupil referral units, youth offending teams, virtual schools and sixth form colleges in England. "
Source: https://www.artsmark.org.uk/

News & Events
twitterTweet this page
pinterestPin this page
Tuesday 23rd of June to Thursday 25th of June
Buxton School is running shorter school days this week from Tuesday 23rd of June to Thursday 25th of June. We aim to operate on your usual timetable on Friday 26th of June. With it expected to reach up to 37 degrees Celsius outside of the school building, many of our classrooms and indoor spaces could become even hotter than this, particularly in the afternoons. These conditions are not conducive to learning when students and staff are in classrooms.
In line with this, Buxton School will be running shorter (truncated) school days this week. All children (except vulnerable students whose parents the school has contacted) will have left the school site by 1:35pm. This will ensure that the bulk of our children’s learning is protected and that they will have had lunch, whilst ensuring that they are not travelling home during the hottest point in the day. These arrangements ensure the health and wellbeing of our community at this time whilst minimising disruption to the children’s education.
All after-school clubs have been cancelled, and adjustments have been made to ensure that children are not spending long periods of time outside in high temperatures. This includes PE.

Breakfast Club
twitterTweet this page

Breakfast Club
A healthy breakfast will give young ones the fuel they need for learning and the energy they need for the physical activities of the day. A good breakfast also helps to avoid the grumbling tummies that cause cravings for unhealthy snacks and poor food choices that can lead to obesity. We also know that attending a school Breakfast Club gets children into good attendance patterns at school and ensures punctuality.
Primary Breakfast Club offers breakfast and daily childcare, Monday to Friday, 7.30-8.40am. The current cost is £3.65 per day (£18.25 per week).
Please complete an application form if you wish your child(ren) to join Breakfast Club.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brilliant Bears - After School Child Care Provision - Buxton School
pageCache.text:
Brilliant Bears - After School Child Care Provision
Buxton School runs our own, in-house after-school Child Care provision called Brilliant Bears for children aged 3.5 years -16 years. This provision started in February 2016 and operates between 3:30pm and 6pm daily.
Your children will be cared for by a qualified team of staff who will offer a relaxing, stimulating and safe environment. Children will be placed in age appropriate small groups and managed by keyworkers. Activities and stimuli will be delivered via the seven areas of learning within the EYFS (Early Years Foundation Stage) framework which include;
A range of snacks will be provided which will include sandwiches, wraps, pitta bread together with fresh fruit, vegetables and a healthy drink.
If your child attends Buxton primary phase we will collect them at the end of the school day. If your child attends Jenny Hammond School they are also able to attend.
The cost will be £14.50 per single session (3:30pm to 6:00pm) or £6.75 for 1 hour (3:30pm to 4:30pm). To enquire, arrange a visit or book places please contact Zanab Arbi on 020 8534 3425 extension 137
